segments.en: So we haven't seen each other in ages.

segments.en: It's been a long time or we haven't gone out for ages.

segments.en: Okay.

segments.en: Trading so basically trading is buying and selling something.

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So you're trading.

segments.en: Okay.

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that's for trading.
segments.zh: 所以这是为了交易。

segments.en: I put in a margin deposit and then I can buy and sell up to a hundred times that much.

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Well, basically a margin deposit is like a percentage.
segments.zh: 好吧，基本上保证金存款就像一个百分比。

segments.en: So he basically puts in a percentage of what he intends to buy.
segments.zh: 所以他基本上投入了他打算购买的百分比。

segments.en: So for example, a margin deposit of a thousand dollars might be $1 or $10.

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So maybe if it's $10, you're talking about a 1% margin.
segments.zh: 所以也许如果它是 10 美元，你说的是 1% 的利润率。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So that's what he means by a margin deposit.
segments.zh: 这就是他所说的保证金存款。

segments.en: And that's why he explains that you don't have to have a large amount of money in order to trade in the foreign exchange market.
segments.zh: 这就是为什么他解释说你不必有大量的钱来交易外汇市场。

segments.en: You just put in a margin deposit and then you can work around that.

segments.en: He explained about how he makes money and how he bought some Chinese renminbi and then he sold it because it appreciated drastically.

segments.en: So he bought it when it was cheap and he sold it when it was expensive.
segments.zh: 所以他在便宜的时候买了它，在它很贵的时候就卖掉了。

segments.en: So when you see this kind of price change, when something goes from cheap to expensive, it's called appreciating.
segments.zh: 因此，当您看到这种价格变化时，当某些东西从便宜到昂贵时，就称为欣赏。

segments.en: Appreciation.

segments.en: So the verb is to appreciate.
segments.zh: 所以动词是欣赏。

segments.en: It's very different from using it in the sense of you appreciate someone, right?

segments.en: Like I really appreciate you.

segments.en: Yeah, no, it's very different.
segments.zh: 是的，不，这是非常不同的。

segments.en: For example, my parents bought a house in 1970 and the value of the house has really appreciated over the last 40 years.

segments.en: And actually just mentioning it while we're on the topic, to appreciate, as you say, is something becomes more expensive.

segments.en: Depreciate.

segments.en: Okay.

segments.en: So for example, at an auction, when someone is selling many old objects or some art, I can bid $100.

segments.en: You're offering a certain amount of money for that product or that service.

segments.en: My asking price is a hundred bucks, a hundred dollars.
segments.zh: 我的要价是一百美元，一百美元。

segments.en: Maybe you don't want to pay that much, but my asking price is the way that I'm going to start.
segments.zh: 也许你不想付那么多钱，但我的要价是我要开始的方式。

segments.en: That's how much I want for it.
segments.zh: 这就是我想要的程度。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So that's your asking price.
segments.zh: 所以这是你的要价。

segments.en: That's how much you ideally want to sell it for, but you can negotiate.
segments.zh: 这就是您理想地出售它的价格，但您可以进行谈判。

segments.en: You are willing to accept maybe a lower offer.
segments.zh: 您愿意接受可能较低的报价。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And what is our last phrase?
segments.zh: 我们的最后一句话是什么？

segments.en: A split second decision.
segments.zh: 瞬间的决定。

segments.en: This is really, really important.
segments.zh: 这真的，非常重要。

segments.en: These words go together very often.
segments.zh: 这些话经常在一起。

segments.en: Split second and decision.
segments.zh: 瞬间和决定。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that basically means that you made a very quick decision.
segments.zh: 所以这基本上意味着你做出了一个非常快速的决定。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Split second.
segments.zh: 分秒。

segments.en: Very fast.
segments.zh: 非常快。

segments.en: It's almost like it's less than a second.
segments.zh: 这几乎就像不到一秒钟的时间。

segments.en: And so a split second decision means a decision in no time.
segments.zh: 因此，瞬间的决定意味着很快就会做出决定。

segments.en: It's very, very quick.
segments.zh: 它非常非常快。

segments.en: So we can actually mix split second with other things, right?
segments.zh: 所以我们实际上可以将瞬间与其他事物混合，对吧？

segments.en: For example.
segments.zh: 例如。

segments.en: Maybe you can say he reacted in a split second and avoided the crash.
segments.zh: 也许你可以说他在一瞬间做出了反应并避免了坠机。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So good for him.
segments.zh: 对他来说太好了。

segments.en: He reacted quickly enough to avoid the accident.
segments.zh: 他的反应足够快以避免事故。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So split second, very fast, very quickly.
segments.zh: 所以瞬间，非常快，非常快。

segments.en: A split second decision, a decision that was made very fast.
segments.zh: 一个瞬间的决定，一个很快就做出的决定。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that's all we have for Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 这就是我们为 Fluency Builder 所拥有的一切。

segments.en: Why don't we go back, listen to this dialogue one more time and we'll be back to talk a little bit more.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不回去，再听一次这段对话，我们会回来多说一点。

segments.en: Hey John, I haven't seen you in ages.
segments.zh: 嘿，约翰，我好久没见你了。

segments.en: What's new?
segments.zh: 最近有什么新鲜事？

segments.en: What have you been up to?
segments.zh: 你最近在忙什么？

segments.en: Pete, nice to see you.
segments.zh: 皮特，很高兴见到你。

segments.en: Well, on top of the norm, you know, life and kids and work, I've actually gotten into doing some trading.
segments.zh: 除了照常忙生活、孩子和工作之外，我最近还开始做些交易。

segments.en: Trading?
segments.zh: 交易？

segments.en: You big guy?
segments.zh: 你大个子？

segments.en: What are you trading?
segments.zh: 你在交易什么？

segments.en: Currencies.
segments.zh: 货币。

segments.en: Currencies?
segments.zh: 货币？

segments.en: As in euros, dollars, pounds and rupees?
segments.zh: 如欧元、美元、英镑和卢比？

segments.en: It's called Forex, foreign exchange.
segments.zh: 它被称为外汇，外汇。

segments.en: The great thing about it is that I don't have to invest a huge amount.
segments.zh: 最棒的是我不必投入巨资。

segments.en: I put in a margin deposit and then I can buy and sell up to a hundred times that much.
segments.zh: 我先存入一笔保证金，就可以买卖最高相当于它一百倍金额的货币。

segments.en: I don't understand.
segments.zh: 我不明白。

segments.en: You're buying and selling money?
segments.zh: 你买卖钱？

segments.en: You got it.
segments.zh: 没问题。

segments.en: Just last night I made $150 US.
segments.zh: 就在昨晚，我赚了 150 美元。

segments.en: Last night?
segments.zh: 昨晚？

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: It's a 24 hour market.
segments.zh: 这是一个24小时的市场。

segments.en: I'd bought some RMB earlier at a low asking price, but last night it appreciated drastically.
segments.zh: 我早些时候以低要价买了一些人民币，但昨晚它大幅升值。

segments.en: So I made a split second decision and sold all of my RMB at an amazing bid.
segments.zh: 所以我当机立断，以一个很好的买入报价卖掉了手里的全部人民币。

segments.en: I've also done some trading with Swiss francs and Australian dollars and Hong Kong dollars.
segments.zh: 我还用瑞士法郎、澳元和港元进行了一些交易。

segments.en: I've made some good profits, but I've also suffered some losses.
segments.zh: 我赚了一些不错的利润，但我也遭受了一些损失。

segments.en: It depends on a lot of factors, just like any other market.
segments.zh: 这取决于很多因素，就像任何其他市场一样。

segments.en: In total I've made about $500 US in the past few months.
segments.zh: 在过去的几个月里，我总共赚了大约 500 美元。

segments.en: You're kidding!
segments.zh: 你在开玩笑！

segments.en: I'm on.
segments.zh: 我在。

segments.en: I'm going to sign up.
segments.zh: 我要注册。

segments.en: So Marco, you have to explain this to me.
segments.zh: 所以马可，你必须向我解释这一点。

segments.en: We're talking about currency today.
segments.zh: 我们今天谈论的是货币。

segments.en: So every nation has a currency.
segments.zh: 所以每个国家都有货币。

segments.en: For example, in the dialogue we learned that India has rupees.
segments.zh: 例如，在对话中，我们了解到印度有卢比。

segments.en: Pounds are in Britain.
segments.zh: 英镑在英国。

segments.en: Britain has pounds and Australia has Australian dollars.
segments.zh: 英国有英镑，澳大利亚有澳元。

segments.en: America has American dollars.
segments.zh: 美国有美元。

segments.en: But you just said earlier that Ecuador has American dollars too.
segments.zh: 但你刚才说厄瓜多尔也有美元。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Actually, Ecuador went through a very difficult economic situation in late 1998, early 1999, where there was hyperinflation.
segments.zh: 实际上，厄瓜多尔在 1998 年末、1999 年初经历了非常艰难的经济形势，那里出现了恶性通货膨胀。

segments.en: So basically there was an inflation that was very, very, very large.
segments.zh: 所以基本上有一个非常非常大的通货膨胀。

segments.en: So that means that the old currency lost its value very fast.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着旧货币很快就失去了它的价值。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So for example, if the currency before in Ecuador used to be sucres.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，如果厄瓜多尔之前的货币曾经是 Sucres。

segments.en: So if 10 sucres was $1, all of a sudden it was 50 sucres was $1.
segments.zh: 因此，如果 10 Sucres 是 1 美元，那么突然间它是 50 Sucres 是 1 美元。

segments.en: It got to the point where goods and services went from $3,000 to $1 to $25,000 to $1.
segments.zh: 它达到了商品和服务从 3,000 美元到 1 美元到 25,000 美元到 1 美元的地步。

segments.en: Okay, so people have bags full of money and it's not really worth anything anymore.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以人们的袋子里装满了钱，这不再值钱了。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So what happened was the central bank couldn't absorb this currency depreciation.
segments.zh: 所以发生的事情是中央银行无法吸收这种货币贬值。

segments.en: They couldn't really regulate prices.
segments.zh: 他们无法真正规范价格。

segments.en: Basically salaries were about the same, so you have a lot less money comparatively.
segments.zh: 基本上工资差不多，所以你的钱相对较少。

segments.en: And so the government decided that there were two options.
segments.zh: 所以政府决定有两种选择。

segments.en: Either they would follow Argentina's example, what they did a couple of years before, and set a fixed rate.
segments.zh: 他们要么效仿阿根廷的榜样，他们几年前所做的事情，并设定了一个固定的利率。

segments.en: So in Argentina, it's $3 to $1.
segments.zh: 所以在阿根廷，它是 3 到 1 美元。

segments.en: Or we would just get rid of our currency and just use US dollars.
segments.zh: 或者我们只会摆脱我们的货币，只使用美元。

segments.en: So that's what they did, right?
segments.zh: 所以这就是他们所做的，对吧？

segments.en: They used US dollars.
segments.zh: 他们使用美元。

segments.en: And now if you ever travel to Ecuador, you will use US dollars.
segments.zh: 现在，如果您去厄瓜多尔旅行，您将使用美元。

segments.en: The same exact bills that you use in the US are the same exact bills in Ecuador.
segments.zh: 您在美国使用的完全相同的账单与厄瓜多尔的完全相同的账单。

segments.en: So no need to exchange currency.
segments.zh: 所以不需要兑换货币。

segments.en: No need to exchange currency.
segments.zh: 无需兑换货币。

segments.en: And that's why I guess there are many factors that people say are a lot better.
segments.zh: 这就是为什么我想人们说有很多因素要好得多的原因。

segments.en: For example, trading has become a lot less complicated because now you're negotiating in US dollars as in everywhere else in the world.
segments.zh: 例如，交易变得不那么复杂，因为现在你正在以美元进行谈判，就像在世界其他任何地方一样。

segments.en: But then other things, as you know, not having a national currency also affects.
segments.zh: 但是，正如您所知，没有国家货币的其他事情也会影响。

segments.en: So there are a lot of things going on.
segments.zh: 所以发生了很多事情。

segments.en: But it's an interesting topic.
segments.zh: 但这是一个有趣的话题。

segments.en: Very interesting.
segments.zh: 很有意思。

segments.en: Well, so maybe for those of you who are listening, you could tell us about your country and your currency.
segments.zh: 好吧，也许对于那些正在听的人来说，你可以告诉我们你的国家和你的货币。

segments.en: What do you use?
segments.zh: 你用什么？

segments.en: What do you spend money on?
segments.zh: 你把钱花在什么上？

segments.en: And do people buy and trade currencies where you're from?
segments.zh: 人们会购买和交易您来自哪里的货币吗？

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Or maybe you can even enlighten us with the exchange rate maybe.
segments.zh: 或者也许你甚至可以用汇率来启发我们。

segments.en: Usually it's a good question to ask how much is a liter of milk or how much is a haircut.
segments.zh: 通常，问一升牛奶多少钱或理发多少是一个很好的问题。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Because these are things that everyone needs.
segments.zh: 因为这些是每个人都需要的东西。

segments.en: So the price doesn't change that much.
segments.zh: 所以价格没有太大变化。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Well, we're really curious to know how inexpensive or maybe very expensive your country is.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们真的很想知道您的国家有多便宜或可能非常昂贵。

segments.en: So come to EnglishPod.com and we'll see everyone there.
segments.zh: 所以来englishpod.com，我们会在那里见到每个人。

segments.zh: 再见。
